use: Sets a condition or trade-off right after agreeing to something.

example.romaji: ii yo. sono kawari, ranchi ogotte ne.
example.ja: いいよ。その代わり、ランチおごってね。
example.english: Sure. But in exchange, you buy me lunch.

examplePolite.romaji: ii desu yo. sono kawari, ranchi o ogotte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: いいですよ。その代わり、ランチをおごってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Sure. But in exchange, you buy me lunch.

notes: Also for a trade-off in facts: yasui. sono kawari, tooi (it's cheap, but then it's far). X no kawari ni = instead of X.

use: Almost always with neru or nemuru.

example.ja: 昨日はぐっすり寝た。
example.english: I slept like a log last night.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou wa gussuri nemuremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日はぐっすり眠れました。
examplePolite.english: I slept really well last night.

notes: Gussuri nemureta? (Did you sleep well?) is a common morning question.

use: Usually furafura suru: feeling faint from hunger, fever or tiredness.

example.romaji: netsu ga atte, chotto furafura suru.
example.ja: 熱があって、ちょっとフラフラする。
example.english: I've got a fever and feel a bit dizzy.

examplePolite.romaji: netsu ga atte, chotto furafura shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 熱があって、ちょっとフラフラします。
examplePolite.english: I have a fever and feel a bit dizzy.

notes: Also drifting about with no aim, or someone who won't commit. A spinning dizziness is memai.

use: Usually kutakuta da or kutakuta ni naru, after a long day.

example.ja: 一日歩いて、もうくたくた。
example.english: I walked all day and I'm totally worn out.

examplePolite.romaji: ichinichi aruite, mou kutakuta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 一日歩いて、もうくたくたです。
examplePolite.english: I walked all day and I'm totally worn out.

notes: Stronger than tsukareta. Also clothes or vegetables gone limp.

use: Usually utouto suru: drifting into light sleep, like on a train.

example.ja: 電車でうとうとしちゃった。
example.english: I nodded off on the train.

examplePolite.romaji: densha de utouto shite shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 電車でうとうとしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I nodded off on the train.

notes: Light sleep, the opposite of gussuri.

use: Almost always onaka ga pekopeko (I'm starving).

example.ja: もうお腹ペコペコだよ。
example.english: I'm already starving.

examplePolite.romaji: mou onaka ga pekopeko desu.
examplePolite.ja: もうお腹がペコペコです。
examplePolite.english: I'm already starving.

notes: Pekopeko suru = bow repeatedly, often meaning to grovel.

use: Usually nodo ga karakara (my throat's parched); also dry air or weather.

example.ja: 喉カラカラ、なんか飲もう。
example.english: I'm parched, let's get something to drink.

examplePolite.romaji: nodo ga karakara desu. nani ka nomimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 喉がカラカラです。何か飲みましょう。
examplePolite.english: I'm parched. Let's get something to drink.

notes: Also a rattling sound, and karakara warau (laugh heartily). A nearly empty place is garagara.

english: queasy, sick to your stomach; seething (angry)
use: Usually mukamuka suru, for nausea or for anger building up.

example.ja: 飲みすぎて、胸がムカムカする。
example.english: I drank too much and I feel sick.

examplePolite.romaji: nomisugite, mune ga mukamuka shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 飲みすぎて、胸がムカムカします。
examplePolite.english: I drank too much and I feel sick.

notes: Anger sense: kao o miru dake de mukamuka suru (just seeing his face makes me mad). Related: mukatsuku (to get pissed off).

use: Usually X ga zukizuki suru, for a headache, toothache or wound.

example.romaji: asa kara atama ga zukizuki suru n da.
example.ja: 朝から頭がズキズキするんだ。
example.english: My head's been throbbing since this morning.

examplePolite.romaji: asa kara atama ga zukizuki suru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 朝から頭がズキズキするんです。
examplePolite.english: My head's been throbbing since this morning.

notes: Handy at a clinic; a sharp stabbing pain is kirikiri, a dull ache shikushiku.

use: Shaking from cold or fear, often buruburu furueru.

example.ja: 寒くてぶるぶる震えたよ。
example.english: It was so cold I was shivering.

examplePolite.romaji: samukute buruburu furuemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 寒くてぶるぶる震えました。
examplePolite.english: It was so cold I was shivering.

notes: Also a phone vibrating.

use: For gentle sunshine, or warmth spreading through your body after a bath.

example.romaji: kyou wa pokapoka shite kimochi ii ne.
example.ja: 今日はぽかぽかして気持ちいいね。
example.english: It's nice and warm today, feels great.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa pokapoka shite kimochi ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はぽかぽかして気持ちいいですね。
examplePolite.english: It's nice and warm today, isn't it.

notes: Always a pleasant warmth, never too hot.

use: Usually jimejime suru, for the rainy season or a damp room.

example.romaji: tsuyu wa jimejime shite iya da ne.
example.ja: 梅雨はじめじめして嫌だね。
example.english: The rainy season is so damp and gross.

examplePolite.romaji: tsuyu wa jimejime shite iya desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 梅雨はじめじめして嫌ですね。
examplePolite.english: The rainy season is so damp and unpleasant.

notes: Mushimushi is hot and muggy; jimejime stresses damp. Also a gloomy, brooding personality.

use: For heavy rain: ame ga zaazaa futte iru.

example.ja: 外、雨ザーザー降ってるよ。
example.english: It's pouring outside.

examplePolite.romaji: soto wa ame ga zaazaa futte imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 外は雨がザーザー降っていますよ。
examplePolite.english: It's pouring outside.

notes: Zaazaa buri = a downpour. Light rain is potsupotsu (a few drops) or shitoshito (drizzle).

use: Usually mushimushi suru, for sticky summer heat.

example.romaji: kyou wa honto mushimushi suru ne.
example.ja: 今日はほんと蒸し蒸しするね。
example.english: It's really muggy today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa mushimushi shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は蒸し蒸ししますね。
examplePolite.english: It's muggy today, isn't it.

notes: Mushiatsui (hot and muggy) is the i-adjective version.

use: Usually gorogoro suru: lying around at home doing nothing.

example.romaji: kyuujitsu wa uchi de gorogoro shiteta.
example.ja: 休日はうちでゴロゴロしてた。
example.english: I just lazed around at home on my day off.

examplePolite.romaji: kyuujitsu wa ie de gorogoro shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 休日は家でゴロゴロしていました。
examplePolite.english: I just lazed around at home on my day off.

notes: Also thunder rumbling (kaminari ga gorogoro), a cat purring, or lots of something lying about.

use: For slacking with no purpose, or something that drags on too long, like a meeting.

example.ja: 今日一日ダラダラしちゃった。
example.english: I wasted the whole day lazing about.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa ichinichi daradara shite shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は一日ダラダラしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I wasted the whole day lazing about.

notes: Gorogoro is lying around; daradara is slack and unfocused. Also sweat or blood running: ase ga daradara.

use: Moving back and forth in one area, lost or loitering; can sound suspicious.

example.romaji: hen na hito ga ie no mae o urouro shiteta.
example.ja: 変な人が家の前をうろうろしてた。
example.english: Some weird guy was hanging around outside the house.

examplePolite.romaji: hen na hito ga ie no mae o urouro shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 変な人が家の前をうろうろしていました。
examplePolite.english: A suspicious person was hanging around outside the house.

notes: Burabura is strolling for fun; urouro is aimless, lost or up to no good.

use: Usually burabura suru: wandering with no plan, or idling without a job.

example.ja: 駅前をぶらぶらして帰った。
example.english: I wandered around near the station, then went home.

examplePolite.romaji: ekimae o burabura shite kaerimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 駅前をぶらぶらして帰りました。
examplePolite.english: I wandered around near the station, then went home.

notes: Also something dangling or swinging, like legs from a high chair.

use: Usually bootto suru (zone out) or bootto shite ita (wasn't paying attention).

example.ja: ごめん、ちょっとぼーっとしてた。
example.english: Sorry, I zoned out for a sec.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto bootto shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっとぼーっとしていました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I zoned out for a moment.

notes: Also feeling dazed from fever or heat: atama ga bootto suru.

use: Usually nikoniko suru or nikoniko shite iru: a warm, steady smile.

example.ja: 今日ずっとニコニコしてるね。
example.english: You've been smiling all day.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa zutto nikoniko shite imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はずっとニコニコしていますね。
examplePolite.english: You've been smiling all day.

notes: Niyaniya is a smirk with something behind it; nikoniko is always pleasant.
